title: Assistant feature idea sprintlet
content:
Goal / one-liner:
Build a tiny, composable assistant feature unit ("skilllet") that product teams can drop into flows for a focused micro-interaction (answer, extract, validate, short action). Low friction: config + small prompt + optional schema + lite telemetry.

Why this?
- Customers keep asking for tiny, embeddable assistant bits (onboarding helper, invoice quick-summarizer, shipping-tracker blurb).
- Full assistant surfaces are heavy; teams want single-responsibility blocks that are easy to test and iterate.
- Helps product teams ship measurable value quickly and avoids over-indexing on huge conversations.

Hypothesis:
If we provide a skilllet scaffold (manifest + prompt template + input mapping + output schema + rollout flags), teams will prototype 3x faster and reduce token costs by 20% vs full-session fallback.

Target users / personas:
- PM/engineer shipping a 1–2 screen embedded assistant interaction
- Solutions engineer building a customer-specific micro-automation
- Platform integrator mapping business data to assistant inputs

Key capabilities (MVP):
1) Skilllet manifest: name, description, input fields (typed), output schema, examples, cost tier hint.
2) Simple editor in Console: edit prompt, example inputs, unit test runner (quick eval), preview UI.
3) SDK + API: instantiate skilllet with a JSON payload. Response validated against schema, optional structured output wrapper.
4) Telemetry: per-skilllet token usage, latency, success (schema match), fallback count.
5) Rollout flags: per-customer enable, canary percent, auto-fallback to baseline model.

User stories (rough):
- As a PM, I want to create a "payment-summary" skilllet that takes a raw payment blob and returns amount, date, vendor so I can show a one-line card in the app.
- As an engineer, I want to call the skilllet via SDK with input JSON and get back validated JSON so I can wire UI components without parsing free text.
- As an SRE, I want to see token and latency histograms per-skilllet so we can set cost budgets and SLOs.

Success metrics (OKRs / acceptance):
- Time-to-prototype: median from "create" to "first successful call" <= 2 hours for internal teams.
- Token efficiency: median tokens per successful skilllet call <= 40 for simple extract tasks vs baseline 60.
- Adoption: 5 internal product teams using skilllets in production within 90 days of launch.
- Quality: schema-match rate >= 95% for validated skilllets after 1 week of live traffic.

API sketch (informal):
POST /v1/skilllets/execute
{ skilllet_id, version, inputs: {...}, routing: {region, model_preference}, trace_id }
Response: { status, output_json, raw_text, meta: {tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, model} }

Console UX notes (quick):
- Editor tabs: manifest | prompt | examples | test-run | telemetry
- Quick test: paste input JSON, run, get colored schema diff + token preview
- Ship flow: Save draft -> canary roll -> enable -> snapshot manifest into deployment revision

Backend considerations (rough):
- Execution path should be lightweight: skip heavy session state. Treat skilllets as single-shot requests with optional caching of recent inputs/outputs.
- Schema validation layer: plug into output post-processing. Failures counted and surfaced. Allow "best-effort" fallback mode.
- Routing policy: can route to cheapest compatible model; provide per-skilllet override for fidelity-tier.
- Autoscaling: skilllet traffic likely spiky (onboarding surges). Default burst policy + reserved capacity hints per-team.

Privacy/security notes:
- Skilllets may accept PII; provide per-skilllet flag for data retention + redaction. Integrate with existing KMS/audit logs.
- Default: do not persist raw prompt examples unless explicitly enabled.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How opinionated should the manifest be? Too rigid -> friction. Too flexible -> inconsistent UX across teams.
- Do we enforce strict schema-only outputs (reject non-JSON) or accept fuzzy text with auto-extraction? Hybrid seems needed.
- Versioning model: manifest + prompt + eval snapshot are needed for repro. Tie to model versions for audits.

Experiment ideas (quick A/B):
A. Strict JSON enforcement vs best-effort extraction: measure schema-match and developer friction.
B. Auto-suggest quantization profile for skilllet by sampling examples -> measure tokens saved and quality drop.
C. Pre-canned templates gallery (FAQ extractor, rate-limit summarizer) vs blank-start: adoption delta.

Risks / failure modes:
- Low developer uptake due to editor friction -> provide CLI + templates.
- Schema mismatch noise -> need strong tooling for example-driven calibration.
- Cost blow-up if teams create many high-frequency skilllets without quotas -> need guardrails and default cost tiering.

Rollout plan (phases):
1) Internal alpha (eng + 2 product teams) — basic manifest + API + test runner (6 weeks)
2) Closed beta with 5 product teams, telemetry + canary rollouts + retention flags (6–8 weeks)
3) Public beta with templates + docs + SDKs (8–12 weeks)

Next actions (short):
- Draft a lightweight manifest schema (Ishaan)
- Prototype console editor mock (Mira)
- Wire a thin API shim calling existing inference runtime, return schema-validated JSON (Drew)
- Create 3 example skilllets: invoice-extract, short-answer-blurb, booking-checker (for demos)

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Ask security if auto-extraction counts as retention.
- Slack thread: summarize concept and ask for 2 volunteers for alpha.
- Save time: mock up test-run UI as a Chrome extension to iterate faster.

Random ideas to revisit later:
- Skilllet marketplaces (internal templates + community contributed manifests)
- Auto-generated example inputs from customer data (privacy-safe sampling)
- Ability to compose skilllets in a micro-orchestration flow (skilllet chains)

End of sprintlet notes. Keep short, iterate.
